chunks: Abu Talib Al-Husayn ibn Abdullah ibn Banan Al-Ta’ee narrated to us, saying: I heard Muhammad ibn Umar Al-Nowqani say:

While I was sleeping in the attic of our house in Nowqan on a dark night, I woke up and looked towards the direction where the Shrine of Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) is located in Sanabad. I saw a light that rose until the Shrine was filled with it, becoming bright as if it were daytime. I was doubtful about the affairs of Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) and did not know that he was right. My mother, who was opposed to him, asked me, 'What is the matter with you?' I told her, 'I saw a radiant light that filled the Shrine in Sanabad.' My mother said, 'That is nothing; this is from the work of Satan.'

He said: On another night, which was darker than the first night, I saw a similar light and the Shrine was filled with it. I informed my mother about this and brought her to the place where I was until she saw the light I had seen, and the Shrine was filled with it. She marveled at this and began to praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, except that she did not believe in it as I did.

Then I headed towards the Shrine and found the door closed. I said, 'O Allah, if the affair of Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) is true, then open this door for me.' Then I pushed it with my hand and it opened. I said to myself, 'Perhaps it was not closed as it should have been.' So I closed it firmly until I knew that it could not be opened except with a key. Then I said, 'O Allah, if the affair of Ar-Ridha is true, then open this door for me.' Then I pushed it with my hand and it opened. I entered, visited, prayed, and gained clarity regarding the affair of Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him). From then on, I would go to him every Friday as a visitor from Nowqan and pray near him until this time.

key_terms.مَشْهَدُ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مُوسَى الرِّضَا: Shrine of Ali ibn Musa Ar-Rida

ai.seo_question: What was the miraculous sign that confirmed the truth of Imam Ar-Rida's leadership for Muhammad ibn Umar Al-Nowqani?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the spiritual authority of the Imam’s resting place, where divine light (nur) serves as a tangible sign (ayah) for believers, particularly in the context of Shia devotional practices. The sequence of doubt, testing, and eventual firm conviction illustrates the Shia epistemological approach to verifying religious truths through personal spiritual experience and divine confirmation. It underscores the shrine not merely as a tomb, but as a locus of divine presence where the boundary between the physical and spiritual realms becomes permeable for the faithful.
